newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss franc ends sharply higher vs dlr, mark.
newsitem.headline: Swiss franc ends sharply higher vs dlr, mark.

text.p: 1545 GMT - The Swiss franc ended up sharply after hitting roughly five-week highs versus both the dollar and the mark.

Traders saw no single fundamental factor behind the move, but noted the dollar's drop below 1.45 francs was negative. Another dealer said some investors may seek to get out of U.S. assets due to worries U.S. interest rates will rise.
One trader believed Tuesday's weakness stemmed partly from a drop in mark/Swiss. Mark/Swiss began by looking bid, trading up to roughly 86.30 centimes before it turned lower.

At the same time, however, Swiss short-term interest rates on the money market were lower, and Swiss National Bank chairman Hans Meyer also said the SNB saw no reason at present to alter its current expansionary policy.

The dollar dropped in Europe to as low as 1.4365 francs. It last traded lower against the Swiss franc on February 12, when it got as low as 1.4329 francs. The mark low in European trade was 85.75. It last traded lower on February 11, when it dipped to 85.59 centimes.
* The dollar ended at 1.4410/4415 Swiss francs versus 1.4563/4569 at the close on Monday.
* The mark ended at 85.80/82 Swiss centimes versus 86.22/24 at Monday's close. -- Zurich Editorial, +41 1 631 7340
